summary_paragraph: A female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus, antiphospholipid antibody syndrome, and end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis was admitted due to progressive weakness and tingling in her limbs, found to be caused by severe hyperkalemia with a potassium level of 8.3. The hyperkalemia was attributed to inadequate peritoneal dialysis over several weeks. She received emergency treatment including calcium, insulin, dextrose, albuterol, and Kayexalate, leading to normalization of potassium and resolution of symptoms. She remained stable, with no signs of infection or dialysis catheter complications. Her lisinopril was held due to hyperkalemia and not restarted given low-normal blood pressure. She was discharged home with medication adjustments, including increased calcitriol and sevelamer, and instructions to follow up with her nephrologist and primary provider for blood pressure assessment.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, benign, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
